title: Simit Sesame Ring Bread

description: Simit is Turkeys beloved sesame-crusted bread ring, a staple for breakfast or a quick snack. Its distinctive crunchy exterior and soft, chewy interior make it irresistibly delicious. This traditional street food offers a delightful taste of Turkish culture, perfect with cheese, olives, or a cup of tea.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the warm water, granulated sugar, and instant dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until the mixture becomes foamy, indicating the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: To the activated yeast mixture, add the all-purpose flour, salt, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Mix with a sturdy spoon or a dough whisk until a shaggy dough forms and most of the flour is incorporated.

instructions.title: Knead and First Rise
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. Lightly grease a clean bowl with olive oil, place the dough in it, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape the Simits
instructions.text: Gently punch down the risen dough to release air. Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a long rope, approximately 20-24 inches (50-60 cm) long. Take two ropes, twist them together tightly, and then join the ends to form a ring. Pinch the ends firmly to seal. Repeat this process for all remaining dough pieces.

instructions.title: Dip and Coat with Sesame Seeds
instructions.text: In a shallow dish, whisk together the grape molasses (pekmez) and 1/2 cup of water to create the dipping mixture. In another shallow dish, spread out the toasted sesame seeds. Dip each shaped simit ring first into the molasses mixture, ensuring it is fully coated, then immediately transfer it to the sesame seeds, pressing gently on both sides to adhere a generous amount of seeds.

instructions.title: Bake the Simits
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 400F (200C). Arrange the coated simits on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until they are beautifully golden brown and have a crispy exterior.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the simits from the oven and transfer them to a wire rack to cool slightly. Simits are traditionally enjoyed fresh and warm, perfect for breakfast or a snack with cheese, olives, jam, or a cup of Turkish tea.

tips: For extra crunch, ensure your sesame seeds are well toasted before coating the simits. You can lightly toast them in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant.
If grape molasses (pekmez) is unavailable, you can substitute it with date molasses or even a thin sugar syrup, though grape molasses provides the most authentic flavor.
Simits are best enjoyed fresh. If you have leftovers, refresh them in a toaster or oven for a few minutes to regain their crispness.
